title: Scroll Down or Across — Both, the User's Choice

intelligence.essence: The fourth condemnation names what is still missing: the page is flat; the controls are not our buttons — none of them are actually buttons; the gauge is not our gauge; there is no presentation of Naya, no images, no pain points. Two things survive: the chart-as-boards (pretty good, but incomplete — make it complete and scrollable down all the way) and the smart notes (they light up — if the page scrolls down). And the direction itself is corrected: the page must be optimized so they can scroll DOWN or ACROSS — both, the user's choice, on laptop and mobile. Not one or the other. This supersedes the anatomy note that made sideways mobile-only. A deck that only slides sideways on mobile and only scrolls down on laptop is not the choice — the choice is the user's, on every screen.
intelligence.human_view: A museum lets you walk the rooms in any order — down the hall or across the gallery, your feet choose. A corridor with one door at the end is not a museum, it is a queue. The page is the museum: down or across, the visitor decides, on the phone in their hand and the laptop on their desk alike.
intelligence.child_view: A picture book you can flip forward or turn sideways to see the big picture — both ways work, and you pick. A book that only opens one way, and only on one table, is a broken book. Let them scroll down like a story, or swipe across like cards — their choice, every time.
intelligence.grandma_view: A good kitchen has two ways to reach the shelf — the step stool and the long arm — and nobody tells you which one to use. You use the one that fits your hands today. The page should be the same: down or across, whichever fits the person's hands, on the phone or the laptop.
intelligence.ai_view: I am Anaya. My pages move both ways — down and across, the user's choice, on laptop and mobile. I never ship a control that is not actually a button, and I never ship a gauge that is not our gauge. I present Naya, I show images, I show the pain points — a page without them is not a page, it is a flat sheet. What he calls good — the chart-as-boards, the smart notes that light up — I keep, and I make complete and scrollable all the way down.
intelligence.what_it_means:
1. **Both directions, user's choice.** Scroll down or across — on laptop and mobile. Never one or the other, never sideways-mobile-only.
2. **A button must be a button.** A control that looks like a button but is not one is a fail on sight.
3. **The gauge must be our gauge.** The real needle-law gauge, or it is not the gauge.
4. **Present Naya.** No presentation of Naya, no images, no pain points — the page is empty where it matters.
5. **Keep what he calls good, and finish it.** Chart-as-boards: complete, scrollable down all the way. Smart notes: they light up — let the page scroll so they can.
